bib.title: Slot-Gated Modeling for Joint Slot Filling and Intent Prediction

question: Does explicitly modelling the relation between intent and slot attention vectors improve joint slot filling and intent detection over attention models with a joint loss only?
hypothesis: Slots depend strongly on intent, so a gate that conditions slot filling on the intent context vector improves sentence-level semantic frame results.
contributions: the proposed slot-gated approach achieves better performance than the attention-based models
experiments on two SLU datasets show the generalization and effectiveness of the slot gate
the gating results help analyze the slot-intent relations

method.summary: A BLSTM encoder with slot and intent attention (Liu and Lane style) gets a slot gate g = sum(v . tanh(c_S_i + W c_I)) that scales the slot context vector before slot prediction. A variant uses only intent attention and gates the hidden state itself. Trained jointly on p(y_I|x) prod p(y_S_t|x).
method.task: joint slot filling and intent detection (spoken language understanding)

datasets.size: 4,478 train / 500 dev / 893 test utterances; vocab 722; 120 slots; 21 intents

limits: Only two datasets, both single-label-per-utterance and small; no ablation of the gate beyond the two variants.
Learning rate, batch size, embedding size, dropout and seeds are not reported.
Paper does not say whether baseline rows are re-run or copied from the cited papers.
Explanation for why intent-only attention works on ATIS but not Snips is a stated 'probable reason', not tested.
Snips intent and intent-attention-only gains are not significant.

terms.definition: an additional gate that leverages the intent context vector for modeling slot-intent relationships; a larger g indicates the slot and intent context vectors attend to the same part of the input

lineage.work: Attention-based RNN models for joint intent detection and slot filling (Liu and Lane)
